{
  "voice_profile": "Third-person autobiography in which the aged author calls his younger self 'he,' 'the boy,' or 'Henry Adams.' It moves between the child's limited view and the old man's retrospective irony. It relies on aphorism and paradox, such as 'Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.' Self-deprecation is played as mock-scientific analysis: variation, type, force, stamp. Long periodic sentences end in a dry reversal. Lists build through dashes and semicolons. Exact dates anchor the account. Qualifiers like 'perhaps,' 'probably,' and 'he could never decide' recur. Every episode is measured as a lesson in education that taught little or the wrong thing. Double hyphens are characteristic and must be kept.",
  "book_context": "The book is a sequence of failed or accidental 'educations,' each measured against what the twentieth century would demand. Chapters I–IV set up the core oppositions. Quincy against Boston, summer against winter, liberty against law, the eighteenth century against the coming age, unity against multiplicity, and Adams against State Street all recur, culminating in the closing dynamic theory of history. Recurring motifs seeded here include:\n- silence and holding one's tongue;\n- the Cunard steamers as signs of the new world and of escape;\n- Sumner as idol, whose later loss teaches that 'a friend in power is a friend lost';\n- the father's perfect poise, tested in London;\n- the four tools, above all mathematics, that he never mastered;\n- the vanished religious instinct;\n- the formula 'Education had not begun.'\nSkipped chapters (Chicago, Silence, Free Fight, President Grant) cannot carry payoffs, so the setups here must be sufficient on their own.",

        {"paragraph": 9, "text": "The world never loved perfect poise. What the world does love is commonly absence of poise, for it has to be amused.", "purpose": "Aphoristic explanation of why the father was called cold."},

        {"paragraph": 16, "text": "All experience since the creation of man, all divine revelation or human science, conspired to deceive and betray a twelve-year-old boy who took for granted that his ideas, which were alone respectable, would be alone respected.", "purpose": "Signature ironic hyperbole about a misleading education."},
        {"paragraph": 19, "text": "Boston had solved the universe; or had offered and realized the best solution yet tried. The problem was worked out.", "purpose": "Ironic summary of Unitarian complacency."},

        "Boston left the mind supple but formless. Women taught only domestic virtues; 'The garden of Eden was hardly more primitive.'",
        "Blackguard Boston and the snowball war on the Common. Bully Hig is struck by a stone. Henry stays only because his brother Charles is too big to run. Conky Daniels sweeps past those who stand. The moral: blackguards not so black. Then the retrospective line on Savage and Marvin.",
        "Violence familiar from mobs, Garrison, Phillips, Parker, and the Fugitive Slave Law. The bayonets in Court Square wrought 'frenzy' in the fifteen-year-old.",

        "The Senate as a friendly club of a Roman species, with Clay, Webster, and Calhoun present. Southern pomposity was genial; he felt more at home than in Boston State House.",

        "The 1851 coalition: Free Soil managers (Wilson, Alley) bargain with the Democrats. The statesmen disdain it yet profit, with Sumner made Senator and Boutwell Governor. The boy's motive was personal; the outcome was lasting moral confusion. 'Tammany Hall stood at the end of the vista.'",
        "The gallery and the 'one-eyed abolitionist' mishearing; the April 24, 1851 vote; running home to tell Sumner, 'the proudest moment in the life of either.'         "Leaving Dixwell's school in June 1854 with 'unqualified joy.' New England boys were 'born too old'; Harvard was attended by custom, not taken seriously.",
        "Harvard's Unitarian 'mesure': it created 'a type but not a will' and left a water-mark. It was the least hurtful university, and left the mind supple.",
        "He got nothing from distinguished mates. Give a condensed portrait of the Class of 1858: negative, self-distrustful, formidable critics, judgment 'a sort of gravitation.'",
        "The Virginians: Roony Lee, son of Colonel Robert E. Lee, with his Petersburg 'staff,' plus Anderson. Lee had the habit of command, was popular, then faded, being 'simple beyond analysis.' Keep the danger of drink and the knife or pistol, and Lee keeping his staff under control.",
        "Adams liked them. He suspected two eighteenth-century types were equally unfit for an economist's America. Both failed, Lee totally and Adams partially. Lee took Winfield Scott's commission against the Mormons and asked Adams to write his acceptance letter: 'The diplomat felt his profession.'",

        "Harvard as a negative force: it weakened political bias. He turned to writing and accepted the instructors' middling ranking.",
        "Lowell opened the door to Germany. The literary world's German faith was a revolt against coming capitalism. Reading privately in Lowell's study was the one gain.",
